text:
Kaedan Korczak picked up two assists against Vegas, the team that drafted him, on Nov. 3, and two more against Boston two nights later. He has 10 assists in 17 games for Pittsburgh. Before this season he had 37 points in 155 career games.

That points rate (1.93 per 60 minutes) is far above what we'd expect from him (0.8 to 1.3), so don't build a house on it. The defensive work is the more durable part. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 97th percentile last season at taking chances away, 41st among 215 defensemen, and the Penguins take 56% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five this year, almost six points better than without him.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flags the weakness: only 29% of his exits keep possession, so he relies on clearing the zone rather than skating it out. He has a big shot (92nd percentile) and no goals yet. He's 25 and played under 20 minutes most nights. We project about 32 points. The interesting question is whether Pittsburgh sees a top-four defenseman here or a good third-pair player on a hot run.
headline: Ten assists and the old team
